newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Member states may impose penalties to enforce EU law.
newsitem.headline: Member states may impose penalties to enforce EU law.

text.p: The European Court of Justice ruled on Thursday Community rules on hazardous waste disposal do not prohibit member states from imposing criminal penalties on offenders under national law.

Criminal defendants challenged Italian law on the grounds that harmonised EU rules should apply. Although Italy did not adopt the directive within the prescribed time, the court said that would only matter if the Italian laws were incompatible with the directive.

The court noted the directive does not impose specific penalty obligations but said member states "must ensure in particular that infringements of Community law are penalized under conditions, both procedural and substantive, which are analogous to those applicable to infringements of national law of a similar nature and importance and which, in any event, make the penalty effective, proportionate and dissuasive."
(Court translation into English. Original language of the class: Italian)

Reference from the pretura Circondariale di Roma, Sezione Distaccata di Tivoli and Sezione Distaccata di Castelnuovo di Port, for a preliminary ruling in the criminal proceedings before that court against
Sandro Gallotti, Roberto Censi, Giuseppe Salmaggi,Salvatore Pasquire, Massimo Zappone, Francesco Segna and Others, Cesare Cervetti, Mario Gasbarri, Isidor Narducci, Fulvio Smaldone
on the interpretation of Council directive 91/156/EEC of 18 March 1991 amending directive 75/442/EEC on waste (OJ 1991 L 78, p. 32)

Article 5 and the third paragraph of article 189 of the EC Treaty must be interpreted as not precluding a member state from imposing criminal penalties to ensure compliance with the obligations laid down by Council directive 91/156/EEC of 18 March 1991 amending directive 75/442/EEC on waste, provided that those penalties are analogous to those applicable to infringements of national law of a similar nature and importance and are, in any event, effective, proportionate and dissuasive.
